paras: The lynching of Scott at Bayou Vidal was the killing of a Black man at Bayou Vidal, Louisiana, on or about August 4, 1900, by people of the neighborhood who suspected him of murdering a farmer. After being repeatedly sunk in the bayou on a chain until he confessed, he was sewn into a weighted sack and thrown into the water. Northern papers carried it as a "New Style of Lynching" because of the method.

According to the New Orleans reports, an old farmer living at Bayou Vidal was murdered some days earlier and his body sunk in the bayou. The Tribune's correspondent gave robbery as the motive and said the body had been weighted with a chain, while the wire account said stones were attached. The wire placed the community in Concordia Parish and described the farmer as white. Suspicion fell on a "strange negro" seen wandering in the neighborhood, whom the wire named only as Scott.

On August 4, Scott was "arrested" and taken to the scene of the murder; the reports name no officer. There he was weighted with chains, thrown into the bayou, and dragged out just before he drowned, and this was repeated several times until he confessed. The Tribune added that the chain fastened around his waist was the same one used to weigh down the farmer's body. After the confession he was sewn into a sack, weighted with stones, and thrown into the bayou at the spot where the body had been found, "where he sunk out of sight."
No report of an inquest, a recovery of the body, or any arrest of the men who drowned Scott appears in the coverage.

The story reached readers through two New Orleans reports dated August 4: a special to the New-York Tribune and a wire account printed by the New York Sun the next morning. The Tribune headlined it "New Style of Lynching" and remarked on its "variations from the accustomed formula," while the Sun ran it as "Drowned Him Like a Beast" over the subhead "Whites Sewed a Negro in a Sack." The Washington Times printed the same wire on August 6 as "Punished by Drowning," and the Arizona Republican reprinted the Sun's version on August 11 under a later dateline.

All of these accounts treated the forced confession as establishing guilt and described the suspect as a "strange negro." The Southern Herald of Liberty, Mississippi, gave the event a single line in its news summary on August 10. No Black-press coverage of the killing was found.

The accounts disagree on the races of the people involved. The wire called the murdered farmer white and the Sun's subhead named "Whites" as the killers, but the Southern Herald reported that "a negro mob lynched a negro for the murder of a negro farmer." The Tribune named the race of neither the farmer nor the killers, and none of the reports gives details that settle the question.

reader.title: Lynching of Scott at Bayou Vidal
bases: Neighborhood residents seized a man suspected of murder, tortured him by repeated submersion until he confessed, and drowned him in a weighted sack (A1, A2, A3); a brief calls it a mob lynching (A4).

The man was sewed into a weighted sack and thrown into the bayou, 'where he sunk out of sight,' by 'the people of the neighborhood' with no trial, as punishment for a murder he was suspected of (A2, A3); the Tribune calls it a 'negro lynching' and the Southern Herald says 'a negro mob lynched' him (A1, A4).

A New Orleans special to the Tribune (A1) and a separately worded New Orleans wire (A2, A3) agree on the core event: a suspect tortured by repeated sinking until he confessed, then drowned in a weighted sack; the Southern Herald brief (A4) agrees on the lynching but differs on the races of the farmer and the mob.

accounts.label: New Orleans special to the Tribune
accounts.gist: An old farmer was murdered for robbery and sunk in the bayou; a strange negro was suspected, sunk repeatedly on the same chain he had used on the body until he confessed, then sewed into a weighted sack and dropped where his victim had been found.

accounts.label: New Orleans wire
accounts.gist: A white farmer of Bayou Vidal, Concordia parish, was murdered; the neighborhood suspected a negro named Scott, who was arrested, taken to the scene, repeatedly sunk until he confessed, and then drowned in a sack weighted with stones.

accounts.label: Southern Herald brief
accounts.gist: A negro mob lynched a negro for the murder of a negro farmer at Bayou Vidal on Saturday.

framing.detail: The Tribune's 'New Style of Lynching' stressed 'some few variations from the accustomed formula' and stated the confession and the chain detail without attribution.
The Sun's headline 'Drowned Him Like a Beast' named 'Whites' as the killers, while the body text presented the neighborhood's suspicion and the forced confession as settling guilt.
The Washington Times ran the wire as 'Punished by Drowning,' framing the killing as punishment.
The Southern Herald gave a single line in a news-summary column, attributing the lynching to a Black mob.

conflicts.note: The two fuller New Orleans reports carry the white version or none; the Southern Herald's one-line brief gives no source.
